import pandas as pd

# Step 1: Define all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/training_9.csv"
]

# Step 2: Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
# Each source has schema ['Id', 'SalePrice']
dfs = []
for path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first numerical index column
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 3: Rename SalePrice columns according to the target schema
# Target schema columns (besides Id) correspond to SalePrice columns from each source:
# Source index to target column mapping:
# 0 -> SalePrice_x
# 1 -> SalePrice_y
# 2 -> SalePrice_x_3
# 3 -> SalePrice_y_4
# 4 -> SalePrice_x_5
# 5 -> SalePrice_y_6
# 6 -> SalePrice_x_7
# 7 -> SalePrice_y_8
# 8 -> SalePrice_x_9
# 9 -> SalePrice_y_10

target_col_names = [
    "SalePrice_x",
    "SalePrice_y",
    "SalePrice_x_3",
    "SalePrice_y_4",
    "SalePrice_x_5",
    "SalePrice_y_6",
    "SalePrice_x_7",
    "SalePrice_y_8",
    "SalePrice_x_9",
    "SalePrice_y_10"
]

for i, df in enumerate(dfs):
    df.rename(columns={"SalePrice": target_col_names[i]}, inplace=True)

# Step 4: Merge all DataFrames on 'Id' using inner join to keep only Ids present in all sources
# This is because the target table has 729 rows, which is less than the largest source (1459),
# indicating an inner join on Id is needed to get the intersection.

from functools import reduce

# Merge all dfs on 'Id'
df_merged = reduce(lambda left, right: pd.merge(left, right, on="Id", how="inner"), dfs)

# Step 5: Ensure correct data types according to target schema
# 'Id': integer
# All SalePrice columns: float

df_merged['Id'] = df_merged['Id'].astype(int)
for col in target_col_names:
    df_merged[col] = df_merged[col].astype(float)

# Step 6: Write the resulting DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_14/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_merged.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
